investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every agent pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent Swarm runtime has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new remote-agent pods at the time of the eval run. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free slots. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing remote-agent pods or other peer-pod workloads, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods. Preemption found no victims, indicating all occupying pods are at equal or higher priority.

[Possible] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes (the 2 kata-capable nodes), and those nodes are at capacity. A misconfiguration or drift in node labels could have reduced the eligible node count below what is needed to absorb concurrent eval probes.

[Possible] A recent scale-down, node drain, or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes from a previously larger pool to only 2, shrinking total capacity without a corresponding reduction in workload.

[Less likely, no direct evidence] A quota or LimitRange applied to the eval probe's namespace could be capping the number of peer-pod VMs the probe service account is allowed to request, causing the scheduler to report insufficient resources even if raw node capacity exists.

investigation.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream, causing the stream to terminate with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame and a valid image URL. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by an exhausted OpenAI billing quota on the account used by the eval runner; no user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI account configured for the eval runner has hit its billing hard limit. When the eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1984) called /api/generate/image/stream with model gpt-image-2, the upstream OpenAI API rejected the request with error code billing_hard_limit_reached. The stream emitted generation_start and generation_progress frames but terminated with a generation_error frame carrying GENERATION_FAILED, so neither the generation_completed frame nor an image URL artifact was ever produced. Both contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — therefore failed. The failure is localized to the eval runner's OpenAI billing credential and the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint; no sibling checks failed and no shared-dependency failure was flagged.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Stale Snapshot (snapshotAgeMinutes=426 exceeds max=300)
investigation.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 426 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot freshness assertion alone.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 426 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-08-04T08:12:10Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 7 hours prior. This is an eval-layer signal of a missed or failed upstream workflow run; no evidence of a user-facing site outage is present — all public page checks passed.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 426' — the sole violated assertion in the contract.
failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=426, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and is structurally valid but is stale.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the exact contract boundary that was crossed.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed with HTTP 200 — the public website itself is reachable, ruling out a broad site or CDN outage.
source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: check config shows statusImpact='informational' and required=false — this failure does not constitute a required check outage.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload, confirming the age value is read directly from the live published artifact.
possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot was skipped, cancelled, or failed silently, causing no new snapshot to be written for at least 426 minutes.
Second: The workflow ran but the publish step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deploy or artifact upload) failed after the snapshot was generated, leaving the stale file in place.

Third: A scheduled workflow trigger was missed due to GitHub Actions queue delays, runner unavailability, or a cron schedule misconfiguration, resulting in a gap longer than 300 minutes between successful runs.
Fourth (lower confidence): A branch protection, permissions change, or secrets expiry prevented the workflow from committing or pushing the updated snapshot file to the GitHub Pages branch.

investigations.title: image-generation-stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream, causing the stream to terminate with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame and a valid image URL. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by an exhausted OpenAI billing quota on the account used by the eval runner; no user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account configured for the eval runner has hit its billing hard limit. When the eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (line 1984) called /api/generate/image/stream with model gpt-image-2, the upstream OpenAI API rejected the request with error code billing_hard_limit_reached. The stream emitted generation_start and generation_progress frames but terminated with a generation_error frame carrying GENERATION_FAILED, so neither the generation_completed frame nor an image URL artifact was ever produced. Both contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — therefore failed. The failure is localized to the eval runner's OpenAI billing credential and the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint; no sibling checks failed and no shared-dependency failure was flagged.
proof: failed-check.message: OpenAI error billing_hard_limit_reached surfaced verbatim in the generation_error frame and in the top-level check failure message.
failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent; imageUrlPresent = false.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=543, far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, confirming the request was rejected immediately by OpenAI rather than timing out.
expected-output.contract: assertions require frameTypes contains generation_completed AND imageUrlPresent equals true — both violated.

source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1999 and :2007: imageUrlPresent is set to Boolean(imageUrl); because no completion frame arrived, imageUrl was never populated, yielding false.
possibleCauses: Primary: The OpenAI billing account used by the eval runner has reached its hard spending limit, causing all image generation API calls to be rejected immediately with billing_hard_limit_reached.
Secondary: The eval runner is using an API key scoped to a project or organization whose billing limit was set too low for the volume of eval runs, and the limit was exhausted before this run.

Tertiary: The AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL environment variable is unset, so the runner defaulted to gpt-image-2 (source-context run-status-probes.mjs line 1986); if gpt-image-2 is a higher-cost model, it may have accelerated quota exhaustion compared to a cheaper model.
Lower probability: A misconfigured or rotated API key is being used that belongs to an account already at its limit, rather than the intended eval-runner account.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval check failed because the runtime test call for model aura-gpt-5-5 returned a 502 Bad Gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable, causing 1 of 2 models to fail and violating the allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0 assertions. The sibling model aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 passed cleanly, isolating the failure to the aura-gpt-5-5 provider path only.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the upstream model provider for aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-08-04T08:04:13Z). The runtime test endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test responded with HTTP 502, wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency and a structured error body containing code=provider_account_unavailable and message="AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This is a provider-side or AURA-to-provider connectivity failure scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 model route, not a broad platform outage and not a user-traffic incident (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every agent pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the Pending state, so the eval runner could not reach the agent creation or readiness steps required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent Swarm runtime has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible for peer-pod scheduling. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new remote-agent pods at the time of the eval run. Preemption was also exhausted ("No preemption victims found"), meaning no lower-priority pods could be evicted to free slots. investigations.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 426 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot freshness assertion alone.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 426 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-08-04T08:12:10Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 7 hours prior. This is an eval-layer signal of a missed or failed upstream workflow run; no evidence of a user-facing site outage is present — all public page checks passed.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all passed with HTTP 200 — the public website itself is reachable, ruling out a broad site or CDN outage.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot was skipped, cancelled, or failed silently, causing no new snapshot to be written for at least 426 minutes.
Second: The workflow ran but the publish step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deploy or artifact upload) failed after the snapshot was generated, leaving the stale file in place.

Third: A scheduled workflow trigger was missed due to GitHub Actions queue delays, runner unavailability, or a cron schedule misconfiguration, resulting in a gap longer than 300 minutes between successful runs.
Fourth (lower confidence): A branch protection, permissions change, or secrets expiry prevented the workflow from committing or pushing the updated snapshot file to the GitHub Pages branch.
